title: Faithful finite-dimensional linear representation of an affine algebraic group
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $G$ be an affine $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then there exist $m\geq1$ and a homomorphism of $k$-group schemes $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}_{m,k}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group] which is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, the map $\rho_A:G(A)\to\operatorname{GL}_m(A)$ is injective; in particular its scalar extension to any field is faithful on all algebra-valued points. No smoothness, connectedness, reducedness or perfectness is assumed.

source.place: Theorem 4.9 and Corollary 4.10, printed p.87 (including the coordinate-surjectivity proof of closed immersion); Corollary 3.35, p.75 (faithfulness). Add a trivial summand if necessary so that the dimension is positive.

proof.text: Put $H=k[G]$. By [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf], $G=\operatorname{Spec}H$ and its comultiplication and counit make $(H,\Delta)$ a right $H$-comodule: the two required identities are coassociativity and $(1\otimes\epsilon)\Delta=1_H$. By [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra], $H$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra, since $G$ is affine and its structure morphism is of finite type. Choose algebra generators $h_1,\ldots,h_r$, using [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]; $r=0$ is permitted. Apply [lem-sfb-comodule-finite-subcomodule] to the finite subset $\{1,h_1,\ldots,h_r\}\subset H$. It supplies a finite-dimensional subspace $V\subset H$, containing these elements, with a coaction $c:V\to V\otimes_kH$ whose composite with the inclusion on the first tensor factor is $\Delta|_V$.

source.place: Theorem 4.9, p.87, first sentence; Proposition 4.7, p.86. Finite generation: Stacks Tag 01T2, lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize, applied to the two whole affine schemes.

proof.text: Choose a finite basis $e_1,\ldots,e_m$ of $V$. This follows directly from [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]: delete dependent members of a finite spanning list until it is independent, solving a dependence for a vector with nonzero coefficient at each deletion. The vector $1\in V$ is nonzero, since $\epsilon(1)=1\in k$ by [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf]. Thus $m\geq1$. Write $c(e_j)=\sum_i e_i\otimes a_{ij}$. The coefficients are unique: under the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], the maps $V\otimes_kH\to H^m$, $v\otimes h\mapsto(e_i^*(v)h)_i$, and $(b_i)\mapsto\sum_i e_i\otimes b_i$ are inverse on generators. Here $e_i^*$ are the coordinate functionals of the chosen basis.

source.place: Theorem 4.9, p.87, basis and coefficient expansion; including 1 makes the dimension positive even for the trivial group.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary] to $(V,c)$. It gives a homomorphism of $k$-group schemes into $\operatorname{GL}(V)$; the basis identifies this with $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}_{m,k}$ of [def-sc-general-linear-group]. Explicitly for each commutative $k$-algebra $R$ and $x:H\to R$, its matrix is $(x(a_{ij}))$, since $e_j\otimes1$ is sent to $\sum_i e_i\otimes x(a_{ij})$. Put $B=k[\operatorname{GL}_{m,k}]$ and $\phi=\rho^*:B\to H$, with affine morphisms as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The coordinate $x_{ij}\in B$ therefore satisfies $\phi(x_{ij})=a_{ij}$: evaluate the displayed point formula at $R=H$ and $x=\mathrm{id}_H$. This is an equality in $H$, without a density assumption on rational points.

source.place: Remark 4.1, p.84, especially its final paragraph; Theorem 4.9, p.87, the image contains the matrix coefficients.

proof.text: The inclusion of $V$ in the regular comodule says $\Delta(e_j)=\sum_i e_i\otimes a_{ij}$ in $H\otimes_kH$. Apply $\epsilon\otimes1$, using the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and the other counit identity from [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf]. It gives $e_j=\sum_i\epsilon(e_i)a_{ij}$. Every $a_{ij}$ belongs to the image of $\phi$, and that image is a $k$-subalgebra, so it contains each $e_j$, all of $V$, and every $h_s$. Each element of $H$ is a polynomial in the $h_s$ by [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and the same polynomial in chosen preimages lifts it through $\phi$. Thus $\phi$ is surjective.

source.place: Theorem 4.9, p.87, displayed counit calculation and coordinate-surjectivity argument.

proof.text: Both $G$ and $\operatorname{GL}_{m,k}$ are affine, the latter by its displayed spectrum construction in [def-sc-general-linear-group]. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] with the single affine open equal to the entire target. Its inverse image is $G$, and its map on global sections is the surjection $\phi$ just proved. Consequently $\rho$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: Theorem 4.9 and Corollary 4.10, p.87; Stacks Tag 01QO, lemma-closed-immersion, condition (3) implies (1).

proof.text: For any commutative $k$-algebra $R$, [def-weil-affine-spectrum] identifies the map on points with precomposition $\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-alg}}(H,R)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-alg}}(B,R)$ along $\phi$. If $u\phi=v\phi$, then for each $h\in H$ choose $b\in B$ with $\phi(b)=h$; it follows that $u(h)=u\phi(b)=v\phi(b)=v(h)$. Thus this map is injective, including for nonreduced $R$ and the zero algebra. For a field extension $K/k$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies the scalar-extended coordinate map with $\phi\otimes1:B\otimes_kK\to H\otimes_kK$. It is surjective: each tensor is a finite sum $\sum h_t\otimes\lambda_t$ and is lifted by $\sum b_t\otimes\lambda_t$ with $\phi(b_t)=h_t$; these maps exist by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. The same precomposition argument for any commutative $K$-algebra proves faithfulness after scalar extension. None of these steps requires smoothness, connectedness, reducedness, or perfectness.

source.place: Chapter 4(a), p.83, definition of faithful representation; Theorem 4.9, p.87. Pointwise injectivity and extension of scalars written out directly from the coordinate surjection.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 4.9 and Corollary 4.10, printed p.87, using Proposition 4.7 (p.86) and Remark 4.1 (p.84).

lean.statement: theorem exists_closedImmersion_generalLinearGroup {k : Type u} [Field k] (G : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj G] [IsAffine G.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [QuasiCompact G.hom] : ∃ (m : ℕ) (_ : 1 ≤ m) (ρ : G ⟶ GeneralLinearGroup (LinearGroupSchemes.Index.{u} m) k), IsMonHom ρ ∧ IsClosedImmersion ρ.left ∧ (∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A], Function.Injective (fun x : (Spec (.of A)).asOver (Spec (.of k)) ⟶ G ↦ GeneralLinearGroup.homMulEquiv (LinearGroupSchemes.Index.{u} m) k A (x ≫ ρ))) ∧ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra K A], Function.Injective (fun x : (Spec (.of A)).asOver (Spec (.of K)) ⟶ (Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))).obj G ↦ x ≫ (Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))).map ρ)
